proposal.observation: Round-2 feedback (rejected, 0.5456->0.5363): lowering enhancing.curvature_threshold to 0.0003 with a further Hough relaxation did not add joint lines in rings 8-10 or on the top/bottom joints; the only new oblique segments appeared as spurious short green/red fragments along the noisy left-edge strip (x<300, y~290-1550), correspondence_f1@15 fell 0.278->0.260, depth_nan_ratio rose 0.195->0.202, and initial_prompt_points.png still shows all 10 centres 'propagated' at y~1520. The detection path is therefore saturated: the K pair is recoverable only in the scanner-adjacent mid-band and per-ring direct detection cannot be forced by stage-3/4 knobs within bounds. The incumbent (round 1) depth_map_viridis.png shows where the remaining proxy loss lives: a large white void in the bottom-right (y>780, x>450 at map scale) with a fragmented, speckled edge of isolated green islands, plus a yellow (high-r) fringe immediately adjacent to that void, a yellow high-r strip along the left data edge (x~40-60) bordering the white left margin, and yellow bolt pockets rendered as white holes. In the viridis scale yellow = large radius (bolt pockets are recessed and read yellow), so the voids sit exactly where r approaches the upper radial gate; a speckled island edge is the signature of points straddling a threshold rather than a clean occlusion shadow. Stage 1 is unlocked with a 20.8 cm centreline residual (gate 10 cm): a centre offset of that size makes r vary around the circumference by ~+/-20 cm, so a fixed radial band clips the high-r side of the lining (toward both floor-side edges of the unrolled map). sam_fill_rate (0.569) is also capped by these same uncovered regions (ring-instance panel is light/uncovered over the bottom-right void and bottom strip).
proposal.rule: d3/d5 (stage_2_denoise -> stage_3_upsample): depth-map hole ratio elevated with holes concentrated where r is largest -> f_over_gate (radial gate too tight on the outer side), propagating via inter_stage_dependency stage_2_denoise.f_over_gate -> stage_3_upsample.f_depth_holes -> stage_5_segmentation.f_over_under_coverage (lining left as label 0). Remediation r_radial_gate_widen: widen [r_inner, r_outer] toward the prior radius_range; here only the outer bound is implicated by the yellow high-r fringes, so widen the upper gate only. The alternative remediation for the root cause (re-fitting the centreline via unfolding params) is stochastic and all three worked examples that moved unfolding jointly collapsed sam_fill_rate and inflated depth_nan_ratio, so the gate is widened instead of re-unfolding.
proposal.failure_mode: stage_2_denoise.f_over_gate (outer radial gate clipping high-r lining; downstream f_depth_holes and f_over_under_coverage)
proposal.rationale: Rounds 1-2 exhausted the detection path (round 1 +0.034 F1 accepted; round 2 further relaxation and denser outliers rejected), so the final round moves the one stage not yet touched and whose symptom is directly visible: the outer radial gate. Setting denoising.mask_r_high to the top of its bound (3.15) admits the high-r lining points bordering the bottom-right void, the left-edge strip and the recessed bolt pockets, which should lower depth_nan_ratio and let the SAM ring/block masks cover the bottom-right and bottom-strip regions, raising sam_fill_rate. Only the outer bound is moved: the inner gate is left untouched so that no inside-tunnel structure (rails, brackets) is admitted, ring_count_error stays anchored by the unchanged vertical Hough band, and the round-1 detection settings that produced the F1 gain are retained (binary_threshold 115, hough_threshold_oblique 30, maxLineGap_oblique 50, pattern_tolerance 12 remain in the incumbent; round-2 enhancing/detecting values are not reused). Beyond the lining radius there is only wall/soil return, so widening r_outer carries little background-leakage risk (f_under_gate), unlike widening r_inner. Expected joint response: depth_nan_ratio down, sam_fill_rate up, correspondence_f1@15 roughly unchanged, ring_count_error 0; if the incumbent already sits at 3.15 the overlay is a no-op rather than a regression.
